for_davis: Three threads that map straight onto your plan. (1) The build stack: DeepSeek Flash-1017 is a legitimately good fast/cheap default you can pair with Claude on the hard stuff — keep an eye on it for sprints 3-5, when you'll want cheap model firepower for your agents. (2) The exam lens: BAND's whole pitch is coordinating parallel coding agents — that's your subagent-delegation and orchestration weak areas playing out as a product category. Study it as live material. (3) The cautionary tale: the OpenCode breach is the API-key hygiene drill made real — separate scoped keys per app, rotate them, check usage dashboards. And the agent lockouts are the environment your future employers are building inside: agents don't get to do everything they can do, only everything they're allowed to do. Build for permissioned access from day one.
headline: Agents meet the locked door era; DeepSeek Flash keeps getting cheaper.

stories.summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on Oct 17, a point update to V4.1 Flash with five more weeks of RL post-training: better reasoning, coding, agent and vision scores, roughly 20% fewer tokens per task, same low prices ($0.15/$0.60 off-peak). The weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope under the MIT license — fully commercial — and the API name stays deepseek-flash so nothing breaks. Its own benchmarks lead DeepSWE v1.1 at one of the lowest per-task costs, and the new Search & Fetch APIs are free through Oct 31 when called via server-side tools in DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex.
stories.title: DeepSeek drops V4.1-Flash-1017: MIT weights, 1M context, built for agentic coding
stories.why_it_matters: A fast, cheap, MIT-licensed model tuned for coding agents is exactly the model layer your sprint 3-5 projects can run on. The HN pattern is telling: benchmarks may favor Claude or Gemini, but people keep reaching for Flash because speed and token efficiency change how it feels to work.

stories.summary: Users of Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots and Instinct agents are being blocked across the web. Yelp allows only agents that pay for its data-licensing program; Delta Air Lines blocks agents from booking tickets; JPMorgan Chase (CEO on the Oct 13 earnings call) and Charles Schwab (CEO Oct 15) confirmed they block agents from account access on security grounds; Amazon shows Muse users pop-ups calling unauthorized agents a Conditions-of-Use violation. Meta's response: turning away a personal agent 'means turning away the customer behind it.'
stories.title: The web starts locking out AI agents: Yelp, Delta, JPMorgan, Schwab say no
stories.why_it_matters: The agent economy runs on access, and access is becoming a paid API or a hard no. This is the practical counterpart to yesterday's FTC subpoenas and Anthropic's misbehaving agents: agents are powerful and increasingly unwelcome. Anyone building agents has to design for permissioned access, not assumed access.

stories.summary: On Oct 17 Meta removed the commercial-terms passage that legal experts (via Nieman Lab) called a 'remarkable provision' — language effective Oct 30 that would have let Meta use 'any content' from a business account's domains to 'train' its products, potentially covering every publisher with a Meta business account. Meta says the consolidated crawling terms only applied to its ads and business products and that its crawling practices haven't changed. The News/Media Alliance had called the terms 'outrageous and probably illegal.'
stories.title: Meta pulls the commercial-terms language lawyers said greenlit AI training on publishers' sites
stories.why_it_matters: The battle over what trains AI keeps getting fought in Terms-of-Service pages, not just courtrooms. This one flipped in 48 hours — a reminder that the data-supply story under every model you use is still being written.

stories.summary: OpenCode, the open-source AI coding agent, reported on Oct 17 that a breach affecting 1.4% of its Console users may have exposed API keys for external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) kept in user workspaces. The company ties the breach to a 'large scale distillation attack' on an old system it was already decommissioning, and emailed everyone affected Saturday morning. It asks them to revoke keys, create new ones, update dependent apps and check recent usage for anomalies. The incident is still open and the company hasn't said how attackers got in or whether exposed keys were used.
stories.title: OpenCode reports breach: some users' API keys may be exposed
stories.why_it_matters: You wire API keys into coding agents for a living now. The drill: separate scoped keys per app, rotate on any suspicion, and watch usage dashboards. This incident is the reason the drill exists.

stories.summary: BAND launched BAND for Developers (Oct 15), a desktop app pitched as a shared coordination layer for multiple coding agents: one shared workspace showing what every active agent is doing, so the developer stops copying context between sessions and tracking who does what. Co-founder Arick Goomanovsky describes users splitting work across agents — one writing code, another tests, a third reviewing — with Claude Code and Codex running side by side. BAND says it leaves the agents in place and coordinates them; which agent harnesses it integrates with out of the box is still undocumented.
stories.title: BAND launches a shared desktop for juggling multiple coding agents at once
stories.why_it_matters: Multi-agent orchestration is one of your CAF weak areas (subagent delegation, orchestration patterns) — and it's now a product category. Watch how BAND frames agent coordination: ownership, blockers, handoffs. That's vocabulary worth borrowing for the exam and for your own agent builds.

tldr: DeepSeek shipped a faster, cheaper MIT-licensed coding model with agentic-coding chops; the web fought back against agents (Yelp, Delta, JPMorgan, Schwab all blocking them); Meta walked back the commercial-terms language that would have let it scrape publishers for AI training; OpenCode disclosed a breach that may have exposed some users' API keys; and BAND launched a coordination desktop for running multiple coding agents side by side.
